Festivals · July · Western

Kundum

The harvest festival that moves along the coast

Kundum is the harvest festival of the Ahanta and Nzema peoples of the Western Region. It gives thanks for food, honours the ancestors and drives out evil, and it moves along the coast from town to town between July and November, so if you miss it in one place you can catch it in the next.

When
July to November, each town in turn
Where
Ahanta and Nzema towns from Sekondi to Axim and beyond, Western Region
Kept by
The Ahanta and Nzema
Also called
Abisa, among the Nzema
Region
Western

Where Kundum comes from

Kundum is both a harvest thanksgiving and a religious festival: people thank God for food, remember their ancestors and ask for protection, and cleanse the community for the year ahead.12 One of the earliest written records of it comes from the Dutch trader Willem Bosman on the Gold Coast around 1700.1

Oral tradition gives two beginnings. In one, a hunter saw dwarves dancing in a circle in the forest and brought their dance home; in the other, Kundum began at Ahanta Aboade, where the ripening of a palm tree’s fruit marked the start of the season.12

How it runs

Each town fixes its own start, so the festival travels along the coast. It lasts about four weeks in each town; for the first three most of the drumming and dancing happens at night on the edge of town, after drummers pour libation at the shrines, and the last week brings the main celebrations.1 Among the Nzema it is called Abisa; from Atuabo to Dixcove in Ahanta, Kundum.1 Axim is often called its heart.1

In 2019, for example, Lower Dixcove held it in July and August, Axim in the second week of September and Busua from October into November.2

Good to know if you go

  • Where: Busua, Dixcove and Axim are on the coast west of Takoradi, with beaches and places to stay.
  • Catch it somewhere: because towns take turns, ask locally which town is celebrating that week.
  • Check the dates: the traditional council sets the days each year, often only weeks ahead. Local radio and the national press carry the announcement.
  • Respect the rites: some rituals are sacred and not for cameras. Ask before photographing chiefs, priests or anyone taking part, and follow what the ushers ask.

Questions people ask

What is the Kundum festival?

The harvest festival of the Ahanta and Nzema of Ghana’s Western Region, giving thanks for food and driving out evil.

When is Kundum?

Between July and November. Each town sets its own weeks, so the festival moves along the coast.

Where is Kundum celebrated?

In Ahanta and Nzema towns on the western coast, including Axim, Busua, Dixcove and Sekondi.
